nodes.summary: LIST COLORING is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a list-coloring instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.
nodes.title: The LIST COLORING decision problem

nodes.summary: A list-coloring instance $(n, E, L)$ is feasible when there is a list $c = (c_0, \dots, c_{n-1})$ of $n$ natural numbers such that for every $v < n$ the number $c_v$ belongs to the $v$-th entry $L_v$ of $L$ (taken to be the empty list when $L$ has at most $v$ entries), and $c_u \ne c_v$ for every edge $(u, v)$ in $E$, where $c_w$ is read as $0$ when $w \ge n$.
nodes.title: Feasible list-coloring instances

nodes.summary: A list-coloring instance is a triple $(n, E, L)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges), and a list $L$ of lists of natural numbers (the allowed colors of each vertex).
nodes.title: List-coloring instances

nodes.summary: The LIST COLORING decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: LIST COLORING is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A list-coloring instance $(n, E, L)$ is well formed when the edge list $E$ has no repeated entries, every edge $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$ and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$, and the list $L$ of color lists has length $n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed list-coloring instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
